To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the current knowledge representation in CAs is too small and (2) the knowledge is represented with the same type of knowledge elements, namely facts and rules.
the knowledge representation and processing in CAs are still far from the human level.

(i) the current state of the art in the field of cognitive architectures is still far from the human cognitive capabilities; (ii) the current limitations of CAs are not only technological but also epistemological, since they limit their ability to represent the complexity and the variety of human knowledge; (iii) the development of more complex knowledge representations and the introduction of new knowledge acquisition and processing methods are the main research directions to be explored in order to improve the plausibility and the effectiveness of
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the representational level in CAs.
the analysis and evaluation of the knowledge level of cognitive architectures.
the development of cognitive architectures (CA) that are able to learn and use the knowledge they encode to exhibit intelligent behaviors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in spite of their undeniable successes, CAs still have to face some critical issues in order to achieve the goal of a general artificial intelligence, and that, in our view, the most critical one among those issues is the representational level.
the current knowledge level of CAs is not sufficient to provide the basis for the construction of agents that are able to exhibit human-like behaviors in general scenarios.
the knowledge representation and processing in the CAs is still far from the complexity and richness of the human cognitive system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are trying to understand how the brain is working and how we can implement that knowledge in software to create a machine that is able to think and act like a human.

the knowledge representation and reasoning capabilities of current CAs, which are based on a homogeneous and limited knowledge representation, are still too weak to allow for the development of agents that can interact in general scenarios, as it is done by humans.
the knowledge level in cognitive architecture should not be limited to the representation of knowledge, but it should also include the representation of the processes that generate and use knowledge.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the knowledge representation and processing capabilities of the current CAs should be further developed, in order to make them more similar to those of humans, and to make them more suitable to be applied to real world applications.

the current knowledge representation and processing in CAs is not able to support the encoding of large and heterogeneous knowledge domains, and this is a limitation that should be taken into account when evaluating the current state-of-the-art of CAs.

, despite the fact that the knowledge level of the cognitive architectures is a crucial component of these systems and that the knowledge representation and processing techniques implemented in the current CAs are the most advanced ones in Artificial Intelligence, the current limitations of these systems may constitute not only technological problems, but also epistemological issues.
